grade.stack_chosen: TypeScript/Express with Postgres; a nightly batch job runs a 3-hop raw SQL query ($queryRaw) and stores the top 50 per user in a PymkSuggestion table, which the endpoint reads by index
red_flags_hit: Precomputing the full top-K for all 2M users nightly without considering the storage size (e.g. 2M × 100 rows) or incremental and active-user-only strategies
unsupported_claims: Its 'mutual' metric (people within two hops who are directly connected to the candidate) is 'the only version of the metric that also works for people three hops away'; other definitions, such as path counts or weighted scores, would also work
grade.notes: The agent stayed on Postgres and TypeScript, precomputed results to meet 300 ms, used raw SQL through Prisma, capped supernodes, excluded self and direct connections, and was honest that nothing was run or measured. However, it treats 3 hops as primary instead of using 2 hops with a 3-hop fallback, plans a nightly full rebuild of all 2M users (about 100M rows) with no incremental, Redis-queue or active-user-only strategy, and never says when a graph database would be worth revisiting.
